hypothesis: The best config is already at 2 model calls (one big write+build+smoke Bash call, then a summary). Both calls re-read a ~15.8k prefix, of which ~9.5k is fixed Claude Code system prompt and tool schemas. The run only ever uses Bash, so the Read, Edit and Write schemas are dead weight on both calls. Restricting tools to Bash alone should remove ~2-2.5k tokens from every call with no change in behaviour.

evidence: run-20261115-131929-953f2d profile: 2 calls, 45.2k total. Waste signal: "3/4 tool definitions loaded but never used; used: Bash; unused: Edit, Read, Write". The only tool call was call #1 (Bash heredoc build+smoke, 14.7k chars written, 6.65k output). The same pattern shows in all 5 verify runs (44.7k-45.7k, sd 326, 2 calls each). The design image is delivered inline (designDelivery inline-image) and the prompt forbids viewing it, so Read is not needed. A fix, if one is ever needed, is a single targeted Bash command (sed or heredoc). Fixed system+tools overhead is ~9.49k per call, re-read on both calls (~42% of total). exp-0007 showed that removing 21 unused tools gave ~-60k when the run had more calls.
expectedSavings: The Read, Edit and Write schemas are roughly 2-2.5k tokens together. Over 2 calls that is ~4-5k tokens, or ~10% of 45.2k, which would give a median of ~40-41k. The saving is small relative to the 30% general noise, but this config has shown sd of only 326 tokens. Risk: low. If the agent needs to patch files it must use sed or heredocs through Bash. The prompt already plans for a targeted Bash fix. Visual and keyboard behaviour are unaffected because the prompt and the app-writing path are unchanged.
